Review Zoom?

Reviewers see Zoom as the dependable default for virtual meetings: easy to join, stable on weak connections, and strong on the basics like clear audio, video, screen sharing, recording, breakout rooms, and large-group calls. Many say it simply works better than alternatives, especially with clients and less technical users. The main complaints are a cluttered, dated interface, bloated settings, annoying updates, and occasional audio or connection hiccups. A few founders also praise Zoom’s SDK and integrations for bots, transcription, and remote team workflows.

Zoom is a reliable video conferencing tool that makes virtual meetings, webinars, and team collaborations easy. It offers high-quality video and audio, screen sharing, and breakout rooms, making it ideal for both professional and personal use. While it’s user-friendly, occasional connectivity issues and the 40-minute limit on free meetings can be drawbacks. Security has improved over time, but privacy concerns still arise occasionally. Overall, Zoom remains one of the best options for remote communication.

Zoom has been a game changer for both work and social interactions. The video and audio quality are consistently great, and it's super easy to set up and join meetings. I love the screen sharing and virtual background features—they make virtual meetings feel more interactive and professional. The breakout room feature is also a big plus, especially for team discussions. While the free version has a 40-minute meeting limit, upgrading to the paid plan removes that restriction. Overall, Zoom is an incredibly useful and reliable platform for staying connected.

#### What's great

I use Zoom regularly for meetings, client calls, and quick collaborations, and it’s still one of the most reliable video platforms available. The connection quality is consistently stable, screen sharing works smoothly, and joining a meeting is simple even for non-technical users — which matters a lot when working with clients.

Breakout rooms and recording are especially useful for presentations and walkthroughs. It’s easy to guide someone step-by-step while sharing your screen, and recordings make it simple to send instructions afterward.

Compared to other tools, Zoom just works — fewer glitches, less setup friction, and people already know how to use it.
